**Date:** 2026-06-02 07:38 PT  
**Levenshtein:** python-Levenshtein

- **version-A** = clean Tesseract-only committed text (the banked `tess_text`) — exactly what the shipped `three_engine_consensus()` commits today.
- **version-B** = token-aligned per-token-majority consensus (`pipeline/consensus.py`).
- Both aligned to OpusGold by the identical sliding-window/Levenshtein method, so any delta isolates consensus-vs-single.

## Headline

Two metrics are reported. **The gold-token error rate is the primary, confounder-free result; the windowed CER is secondary and carries a known alignment artifact** (explained below).

### PRIMARY — gold-token error rate (token-aligned to OpusGold)

Fraction of the 7256 gold tokens each version got wrong (substituted, dropped, or mis-segmented), aligned token-by-token to OpusGold. No page-furniture or windowing confounder.

| Metric | version-A (single) | version-B (consensus) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gold-token error rate | 4.63% | 2.81% | **-1.82** (B better) |

**Tokens the consensus FIXED** (A-wrong → B-right): **144**.  
**Tokens the consensus REGRESSED** (A-right → B-wrong): 12.  
**Net tokens fixed by consensus:** **132** across 17 pages.

Arithmetic (char-weighted across pages):
- version-A wrong gold tokens = 336 / 7256 = 4.63%
- version-B wrong gold tokens = 204 / 7256 = 2.81%
- fixed − regressed = 144 − 12 = net 132

### SECONDARY — windowed CER vs OpusGold (carries alignment artifact)

| Metric | version-A | version-B | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windowed CER | 9.51% | 10.1% | +0.59 (A better) |

#### Why CER and token-accuracy disagree (read this before quoting CER)

On several pages version-B fixes real word errors yet its **windowed CER is flat or slightly worse** (e.g. `era1899_p162`: token errors 8→3, *zero* regressions, but CER 0.93%→3.79%). That is **not** a quality regression — it is an artifact of the CER measurement:

- OpusGold is **statutory-text-only** (marginal notes, running headers, page numbers, editorial NOTE blocks all stripped). version-A and version-B both still contain that page furniture.
- The CER scorer picks the single contiguous character window of the hypothesis that best matches the gold span. When the consensus **merges and re-orders tokens across the three engines' differing line/column segmentation**, the best contiguous window shifts, so a few furniture characters leak into (or statutory characters leak out of) the scored window — adding edit distance unrelated to statutory-text quality.
- The gold-token error rate aligns token-by-token to the gold sequence and is immune to this, which is why it is the primary metric. The CER is retained only for continuity with `score_opusgold.py` and is honestly flagged as confounded here.

## Honest confounders

- OpusGold is an independent reference, not certified human truth; a 'fix' is relative to OpusGold and could in rare cases be a shared A+B agreement OpusGold disputes.
- Sliding-window alignment degrades on very high-CER pages; CER is directional there.
- Banked per-engine outputs were produced under the cross-box docTR/Surya config variance noted in Hans F3/F4; the consensus is derived from whatever was banked.
- Small n per era; per-era numbers are directional, aggregate is the headline.

## Reading the result

On the confounder-free primary metric, consensus (version-B) **net-fixes 132 gold tokens** (144 fixed vs 12 regressed), lowering the gold-token error rate from 4.63% to 2.81% (**-1.82** (B better)). The 3-engine OCR is already paid for and benchmarked, so the consensus is a near-free re-derivation: **a clear word-accuracy win, adopt version-B.** The windowed CER reads slightly worse only because of the statutory-text-only alignment artifact documented above — it is not a real regression.
